title: The Second Shift
description: After losing his decades-long factory job, an experienced machinist learns to carve wooden toys for local children.
character_reference: a weathered man with deep laugh lines around his eyes, wearing a faded plaid flannel shirt and canvas work apron

scenes.narration: The factory lights clicked off for the very last time, leaving behind a silence that echoed louder than any machinery.
scenes.visual: dim industrial workshop with heavy shadows cast by idle steel presses and empty workbench surfaces

scenes.narration: My hands were used to tightening bolts and calibrating steel, but empty palms felt strangely light and terrifying.
scenes.visual: close-up of calloused hands turning over slowly in a shaft of pale afternoon light coming through a dusty window

scenes.narration: In the corner of my small garage, a block of soft pine sat waiting for a purpose far simpler than any engine part.
scenes.visual: workbench surface piled with wood shavings holding a single rough square block of pale yellow pine wood

scenes.narration: I picked up a whittling knife, letting muscle memory guide the blade through the fragrant, yielding wood.
scenes.visual: close-up of a sharp pocketknife slicing a long, curling ribbon of fragrant light wood from a pine block

scenes.narration: Slowly, the block took the shape of a clumsy little wooden horse with sturdy legs and a proud, rounded neck.
scenes.visual: hands smoothing the rough edges of a small handmade wooden toy horse using fine-grained sandpaper

scenes.narration: When a neighborhood child smiled at the unfinished toy, I realized my working life was only beginning anew.
scenes.visual: close-up of a smiling child's small hand reaching out to touch a polished wooden horse on a rustic wooden table

scenes.narration: Every ending makes room for something handmade and true. Follow along for more stories of fresh starts.
scenes.visual: warm glowing workshop interior filled with rows of wooden toys drying under soft incandescent work lamps
